title: Introducing Hurdle: Run agent evals on your API, skills, and docs
gist: Together AI open-sourced Hurdle, an npm library that runs Claude Code and Codex against prompt-style tasks on a company's API, skills and docs, scoring each run with code checks, blocking guards and an LLM judge across model/condition/repeat grids. Sandboxed runs on the Together Sandbox API route all agent traffic through a local proxy (Guardian) that swaps in real keys and enforces guards, positioning 'agent experience' evals as a new developer-platform discipline that also pulls usage onto Together's sandbox product.

themes.theme: Agents as the API's main user

insights.claim: Together AI argues that coding agents are now one of the main ways developers access an API, SDK and docs, so platforms must benchmark how well agents can use them on real-world tasks.
insights.speaker: Mo King, Sam Barrowclough, Hassan El Mghari
insights.so_what: Developer-tool companies that do not optimize for agent usability risk losing adoption as agents become the primary integration layer.
insights.quote: coding agents are one of the main ways devs access your API, SDK, and docs

insights.claim: Together AI spent six months building Hurdle after finding that orchestrating agent evals by hand across models, harnesses and conditions was extremely tedious, and has now open-sourced it as an npm library.
insights.speaker: Mo King, Sam Barrowclough, Hassan El Mghari
insights.so_what: Signals 'agent experience' (AX) evaluation is emerging as a tooling category; watch for competing eval frameworks from API-first companies.
insights.locator: To automate the process, we spent the last six months

insights.claim: Hurdle scores agent runs three ways that can be mixed: deterministic code checks on API requests and produced files, guards that block forbidden actions (e.g. launching an expensive GPU cluster) and count any attempt as failure, and an LLM judge grading the recorded session against a plain-English rubric.
insights.speaker: Mo King, Sam Barrowclough, Hassan El Mghari
insights.so_what: A reusable template for measuring whether agents use a platform correctly and safely, not just whether they finish.
insights.locator: Exactly how scoring works is up to you

insights.claim: Hurdle runs every task against every agent/model combination and condition (e.g. with vs. without a company's MCP server or skill installed) and repeats each combo multiple times to produce a pass rate, because agents do not behave the same way twice.
insights.speaker: Mo King, Sam Barrowclough, Hassan El Mghari
insights.so_what: Lets platforms quantify the ROI of shipping MCP servers and agent skills, an increasingly common developer-relations investment.
insights.quote: Agents don’t always run the same way twice
insights.locator: You can also run each task under different conditions

insights.claim: Together's example suite tested its GPU-cluster task on claude-opus-4-8 and claude-sonnet-4-6, with and without a GPU-clusters skill, 15 repeats each, for 60 runs, using a hybrid verdict where both code checks and an Opus judge must pass.
insights.speaker: Mo King, Sam Barrowclough, Hassan El Mghari
insights.so_what: Shows API vendors already benchmark agent usability on frontier Anthropic models; the results viewer tracks pass rate, duration and cost per run.

insights.claim: The authors recommend starting by picking one task users already give their agents, adding a check, and running it on the best available model plus one a tier below, repeated several times since any single run can pass or fail by chance.
insights.speaker: Mo King, Sam Barrowclough, Hassan El Mghari
insights.so_what: Practical heuristic: model-tier comparison reveals whether platform docs are robust enough for cheaper agents.
insights.locator: After that, pick one task your users are already giving

insights.claim: Local Hurdle runs cannot see or block the agent's API requests and execute as the user with access to local files and real API keys, so Together advises using a sandbox for anything complex or risky.
insights.speaker: Mo King, Sam Barrowclough, Hassan El Mghari
insights.so_what: Agent safety constraints push eval and agent workloads toward hosted sandboxes, a growing infrastructure niche.
insights.quote: For anything complex or risky, you should always use a sandbox.
insights.locator: Local runs come with two caveats

insights.claim: Sandboxed Hurdle runs use the Together Sandbox API to boot a fresh isolated environment per run with no network access of its own; all connections tunnel over a WebSocket back to a local proxy called Guardian that allows or rejects each request.
insights.speaker: Mo King, Sam Barrowclough, Hassan El Mghari
insights.so_what: Hurdle doubles as a distribution channel for Together's sandbox product, converting eval demand into paid compute usage.

insights.claim: Guardian keeps secrets out of the sandbox by giving the agent random stand-in keys and swapping in the real key only on forwarded requests (Authorization header only), and answers guarded requests with a 403 so they never reach the API.
insights.speaker: Mo King, Sam Barrowclough, Hassan El Mghari
insights.so_what: A credential-isolation pattern for agents that is likely to be copied in agent security tooling.
insights.quote: Your keys never enter the sandbox
insights.locator: Your keys never enter the sandbox

insights.claim: By default the Hurdle sandbox does not limit which endpoints an agent can call, so Together recommends a dedicated low-balance key plus guards for dangerous actions; the Together side of each sample run costs only a fraction of a cent.
insights.speaker: Mo King, Sam Barrowclough, Hassan El Mghari
insights.so_what: Agent evals are cheap per run on the infra side; model-provider tokens dominate cost.
insights.locator: By default, the sandbox doesn't limit which endpoints
